questions.q: Where does the safety case concept originate?
options: It was invented specifically for AI governance in 2023
Older safety-critical industries such as aviation and nuclear power, which require structured, evidence-backed arguments that a system is acceptably safe in a specific context
It originated from Google's 2018 model card paper
It is a purely theoretical idea with no precedent outside AI
questions.explain: Safety cases are a long-established practice borrowed from safety-critical industries like aviation and nuclear power, where regulators require structured, evidence-backed safety arguments.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a responsible scaling framework and a deployment safety case?
options: A safety case is written before a framework exists, and the framework is written afterward to match it
A responsible scaling framework only applies to deployed models, while a safety case only applies to models still in training
They are the same document under two different names

A responsible scaling framework sets capability thresholds in advance for future models in general; a safety case argues, with evidence, that one specific model at one specific decision point meets them
questions.explain: An RSP sets the bar in advance; a safety case is the specific, evidence-backed argument that a particular model actually clears that bar.

questions.q: What is an "inability argument" in the context of an AI deployment safety case?
options: An argument that the model should never be deployed under any circumstances
An argument that evaluation results are inherently unreliable
An argument that monitoring systems are unable to detect any problems
An argument asserting, with evidence, that the model lacks the capability needed to cause a specific harm in the first place
questions.explain: An inability argument shows the model simply doesn't have the relevant capability, as opposed to a control argument, which grants the capability might exist but argues safeguards contain it.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about the current maturity of frontier AI safety case methodology?
options: It is a fully solved, standardized practice used identically across all labs
A comprehensive, scalable safety case methodology for frontier AI does not yet exist; researchers have proposed narrower templates as proofs of concept rather than finished solutions
It was fully resolved by the original 2018 model card paper
Safety cases have been entirely abandoned as impractical
questions.explain: Researchers studying the problem have been explicit that a holistic safety case isn't feasible with today's tools, making this a genuinely active and immature area of safety research.

questions.q: What kinds of evidence does an AI deployment safety case typically draw on, per this lesson?
options: Capability/safety evaluation results, red-teaming findings, interpretability evidence where available, and monitoring/response plans
Only marketing materials about the model's intended use
A single overall risk score with no supporting detail
Exclusively financial projections for the deployment
questions.explain: A safety case assembles evaluation results, red-teaming findings, interpretability evidence, and post-deployment monitoring plans into a structured, evidence-backed argument.
